questions.question: On a road with no sidewalks, where should a pedestrian walk?

options.text: On the side with the lightest traffic.
On the same side traffic is moving.
On the side facing oncoming traffic.
On the side with the heaviest traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side facing oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Walk on the side of the road facing the traffic nearest to you. This lets drivers see you coming.

questions.question: What causes "highway hypnosis"?

options.text: Staring at the road for a long time.
Taking frequent rest stops.
Getting too much sleep the night before.
Driving short trips on expressways.

questions.correctAnswerText: Staring at the road for a long time.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare straight ahead and stop looking around. You zone out and may not notice traffic slowing or stopping in front of you.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spot when changing lanes?

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Use your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Mirrors cannot show all blind spots. Always turn your head and look over your shoulder before changing lanes.

questions.question: When must you stop for a school bus with red lights flashing?

options.text: Until all students are off the bus.
Until the stop arm is pulled back.
Until the stop arm is pulled back and the bus starts moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Until the stop arm is pulled back and the bus starts moving.
questions.explanation: Stay stopped until the red lights turn off, the stop arm is pulled back, and the bus begins moving again.

questions.question: What should you do if you are in another driver's blind spot?

options.text: Move forward or back so the driver can see you.
Keep driving at the same speed.
Stay in the blind spot.
Honk your horn to alert them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or back so the driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Never stay in someone else's blind spot. Move ahead or fall back so they can see you.

questions.question: Why do large trucks need extra space in front?

options.text: So other drivers can merge onto the freeway.
So the truck can stop.
So other drivers can slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: So the truck can stop.
questions.explanation: Large trucks take longer to stop than cars. Do not pull in front of a truck and then slow down or stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Falling rocks
Trucks use second gear
Steep hill

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep hill
questions.explanation: This yellow and black warning sign tells you a steep hill is ahead. Slow down and shift to a lower gear to protect your brakes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A lane is ending.
No right turn.
Slippery when wet.
Two-way traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: A lane is ending.
questions.explanation: This yellow and black warning sign tells drivers that a lane is ending. Be ready for traffic to merge safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The right lane ends and traffic must merge left.
The road curves ahead.
Intersections are coming up.
Road construction is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends and traffic must merge left.
questions.explanation: This sign means the right lane on the road ends ahead. Cars in the right lane must move to the left.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A sharp right turn is ahead.
A road joins from the right.
The road turns sharp right then sharp left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road turns sharp right then sharp left.
questions.explanation: This yellow and black warning sign means the road ahead will turn sharply right and then sharply left.

questions.question: How should drivers check for objects in their blind spots when changing lanes?

options.text: Only look in the left outside mirror.
Look over your left or right shoulder.
Only look in the inside rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your left or right shoulder.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Look over the correct shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: At a stop sign with no crosswalk, must you stop before entering the intersection?

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, you must come to a complete stop at the stop line if one exists. If there is no stop line, stop before entering the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Slam on the brakes.
Hold the steering wheel firmly and slow down to a stop.
Keep driving normally.
Turn on emergency flashers and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly and slow down to a stop.
questions.explanation: Do not brake immediately. Grip the steering wheel firmly and stay in your lane. Slow down gradually by taking your foot off the gas. Once you are moving slowly, apply the brakes lightly and pull off the road safely.

questions.question: Before driving, remove snow, frost, and ice from:

options.text: Just the windshield.
All windows.
Just the windshield and passenger window.

questions.correctAnswerText: All windows.
questions.explanation: You must see clearly through all windows before driving. Remove all snow, ice, and frost from every window and mirror.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, when should you return to your original lane?

options.text: When you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
Once you have cleared the front bumper of the other vehicle.
When you are 50 feet in front of the other vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Return to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. This gives you enough space to safely move back in front.

questions.question: On a freeway, why should you look farther ahead than on a city street?

options.text: To spot hazards early.
Because it takes a quarter mile to stop your vehicle.
To keep up with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: To spot hazards early.
questions.explanation: On the freeway, watch for traffic changes and signals from other drivers. Be ready for vehicles merging at on-ramps and changes in road conditions.

questions.question: You are in an accident and another person is injured. What should you do?

options.text: Move the injured person away immediately.
Never move the injured person.
Don't move the injured unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't move the injured unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move injured people unless it is necessary. Moving them the wrong way can make injuries worse. Keep them warm until help arrives. If there is heavy bleeding, apply direct pressure to stop it.

questions.question: When entering an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Stop, check for cars, and enter when safe.
Check for cars and slow to 25 mph before entering.
Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when safe.
questions.explanation: Don't stop when entering an interstate. Use the acceleration lane to speed up and match the traffic flow, then merge smoothly into traffic.

questions.question: A police officer directs you to go through a red traffic light. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to turn green.
Go through without stopping.
Come to a complete stop first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go through without stopping.
questions.explanation: A police officer's directions always override traffic signals and signs. Follow the officer's instructions.

questions.question: A bicyclist who breaks traffic laws:

options.text: Is allowed to because bicyclists don't have to follow traffic laws.
Can receive a ticket.
Will always get only a warning.
Will have their bicycle taken away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can receive a ticket.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers. Both bicyclists and drivers can be ticketed for breaking traffic laws.

questions.question: When using a roundabout, what should drivers do?

options.text: Stop inside the roundabout.
Yield to cars entering the roundabout.
Drive clockwise around the circle.
Yield to cars already in the roundabout.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to cars already in the roundabout.
questions.explanation: A roundabout is a circular intersection with no traffic signal. Cars move counterclockwise around a center island. When entering, you must yield to cars already in the roundabout. Then follow the circle until you reach your exit.

questions.question: What do yellow lines separate?

options.text: Traffic lanes on one-way streets.
Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
All carpool lanes from regular lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of roads with two-way traffic. A solid yellow line means you cannot cross to pass. A broken yellow line means you can cross to pass if it is safe and does not interfere with other traffic.

questions.question: If a train is close or moving fast enough to be dangerous, what must you do?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Do not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.
Cross the tracks at your own risk.
Find a different route to cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.
questions.explanation: Always look and listen for trains before crossing railroad tracks. If a train is near or going fast enough to be dangerous, you cannot cross. This applies even if there are no signals or the signals are broken.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in fog?

options.text: Parking lights.
Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
It does not matter which lights you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: Which statement describes how defensive drivers think?

options.text: They trust that other drivers will do the right thing.
They think about what other drivers might do and prepare to react.
They expect no mercy and give none.

questions.correctAnswerText: They think about what other drivers might do and prepare to react.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means expecting mistakes from other drivers and being ready to respond to them safely.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks affect your driving ability?

options.text: Three
Two
One

questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Do not drive after drinking any alcohol. Even one drink will affect your driving ability.

questions.question: A driver entering traffic from a driveway or private road should:

options.text: Have the right-of-way.
Yield to drivers already on the public road.
Force their way into traffic.
Assume other drivers will move to make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to drivers already on the public road.
questions.explanation: If you are entering traffic from a driveway or private road, you must yield to drivers already on the public road. Merge safely when possible.

questions.question: When a school bus is picking up or dropping off children, you must:

options.text: Stop, no matter which direction you are traveling.
Stop only if you are driving in the same direction.
Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, no matter which direction you are traveling.
questions.explanation: When a school bus is picking up or dropping off children, you must come to a complete stop before reaching it. This applies regardless of your direction of travel.

questions.question: A "No stopping" sign means you may stop only:

options.text: Long enough to unload packages.
To avoid conflict with other traffic.
To let passengers out.
For less than five minutes.

questions.correctAnswerText: To avoid conflict with other traffic.
questions.explanation: A "No stopping" sign means you can only stop to obey a traffic signal, follow a police officer's directions, or prevent a crash with another vehicle.

questions.question: Where can drivers make a U-turn?

options.text: On a freeway
Near the top of a hill
In the middle of a curve
Where it will not disrupt traffic

questions.correctAnswerText: Where it will not disrupt traffic
questions.explanation: A U-turn is a 180-degree turn that reverses your direction. You may only make a U-turn if you can do it safely without disrupting other traffic.
